translation_en: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, Muhammad ibn Rafi', and 'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us. Ibn Rafi' said: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us; the other two said: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from 'Urwah, from 'A'ishah, that they were then seeking the land at Fadak and their share from Khaybar. Abu Bakr said to them: I heard the Messenger of Allah. He related a hadith with a meaning like 'Uqayl's report from al-Zuhri, except that it says: Then 'Ali stood, affirmed Abu Bakr's right, and mentioned his virtue and precedence. Then he went to Abu Bakr and pledged allegiance to him. The people came to 'Ali and said: You did well and acted rightly. The people were close to 'Ali when he approached the recognized course of affairs.

Ibn Numayr narrated to us: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: my father narrated to us. Another chain: Zuhayr ibn Harb and al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Hulwani narrated to us: Ya'qub, Ibn Ibrahim, narrated to us: my father narrated to us, from Salih, from Ibn Shihab. 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr informed me that 'A'ishah, wife of the Prophet, told him that Fatimah daughter of the Messenger of Allah asked Abu Bakr, after the Messenger of Allah's death, to divide for her the inheritance from what the Messenger of Allah had left of the property Allah had granted him. Abu Bakr said to her: The Messenger of Allah said: We are not inherited; what we leave is charity. He said: She lived six months after the Messenger of Allah. Fatimah kept asking Abu Bakr for her share of what the Messenger of Allah had left from Khaybar, Fadak, and his charity at Madinah. Abu Bakr refused her request and said: I will not leave anything the Messenger of Allah used to do without doing it myself. I fear that if I leave anything of his practice, I will go astray. As for his charity at Madinah, 'Umar handed it over to 'Ali and al-'Abbas, and 'Ali prevailed in taking charge of it. As for Khaybar and Fadak, 'Umar retained them and said: They are the charity of the Messenger of Allah, reserved for his needs and the contingencies that arose for him; their administration belongs to whoever holds authority. They have remained so to this day.

Yahya ibn Yahya said: I read to Malik, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah said: My heirs will not divide even a dinar. Whatever I leave after the maintenance of my wives and the expenses of my worker is charity.
Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Abi 'Umar al-Makki narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu al-Zinad, with this chain, with something similar.

Ibn Abi Khalaf narrated to me: Zakariyya ibn 'Adi narrated to us: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Yunus, from al-Zuhri, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, who said: We are not inherited; what we leave is charity.

Yahya ibn Yahya and Abu Kamil Fudayl ibn Husayn both reported from Sulaym. Yahya said: Sulaym ibn Akhdar informed us: 'Ubaydullah ibn 'Umar narrated to us: Nafi' narrated to us, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar, that the Messenger of Allah allotted two shares to the horse and one share to the man from the additional spoils.
Ibn Numayr narrated this to us: my father narrated to us: 'Ubaydullah narrated to us with this chain, with the like of it, but he did not mention the additional spoils.
